text: The fourth dawn rose the color of old copper.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik had not slept. The mark on his palm had throbbed through the night in time with his heartbeat, steady enough that the edges of the world felt thinner than they should. He kept the hand wrapped and told the others it was rope burn. They pretended to believe him.
speaker: Narrator

text: The donkeys had changed. By morning both animals refused the western slope of the dune where they had camped. They pulled against the ropes until the leather creaked, ears pinned flat. Balag crouched beside the nearer one and ran a hand down its neck. The animal trembled under his palm.

text: They know they're donkeys. That's already more than most men.

speaker: Narrator

text: They broke camp without discussion and moved east. The donkeys settled once the western slope was behind them, though Balag kept glancing back. The desert stretched in every direction, a field of gold and red broken only by stone outcroppings and the skeletal remains of old caravan routes. The farther they traveled from Uruk, the less the world seemed to belong to people.
speaker: Narrator

text: By midmorning the heat pressed down through their clothing and wrapped itself around the backs of their necks. Zik walked for part of the day to spare the animals. Ninsun rode in silence, filling the margins of her parchment with notes. She had stopped trying to hide what she was writing. The spiral-drop mark appeared again and again, copied from memory in different forms—some precise, some distorted, one containing a second shape buried inside the first.

text: At first Zik thought it was wind. The noise was so low he felt it more than heard it—a vibration passing through the stone beneath his hand. The dune beyond the rock spine shivered. Sand slipped down its slope in thin streams. Every grain around their boots began to tremble. Tiny ripples crossed the surface of every waterskin. The fire flattened, every flame leaning toward the earth as though something below were drawing breath.
